en.name: Bede the Venerable
en.summary: English Benedictine monk and Doctor of the Church whose Ecclesiastical History of the English People remains the foundational source for early English history.
en.body: Bede entered a Benedictine monastery in northern England as a child of seven and spent virtually his entire life there, dedicating himself to an extraordinary output of scholarly writing across biblical commentary, chronology, natural science, and history, all produced within the walls of a single monastic community rather than through the extensive travel typical of many scholars of his era. His most enduring achievement, the Ecclesiastical History of the English People, completed in 731, remains the single most important surviving source for the history of early Anglo-Saxon England and the conversion of its kingdoms to Christianity, written with a historian's careful attention to sources and evidence unusual for the period. He was also highly influential in popularizing the practice of dating years from the birth of Christ, the Anno Domini system still in common use today, through his historical and chronological writings. He died in 735, reportedly dictating the final lines of a translation to a scribe as he took his last breaths, and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1899, one of very few Englishmen so honored.
